items.title: The Fourfold Refutation: Not Self-Made, Not Other-Made, Not Both, Not Uncaused

items.en: "Nothing produces its own action by itself": because it depends on being drawn out by good or bad companions, by others. "Nor is it produced by another": because it depends on being brought to completion by one's own effort. "Nor does anything else have the power to produce it": because it depends on the specific prior cause, the preceding link having arisen — only then does anything come to be produced.

items.zh: 非內亦非外」等頌中，顯依未來不生雜染；依止現在、過去諸行能生雜染。設行已生，即由此相無有分別；未來無相，故無分別。如此如是當來決定不可知故。若不如是分別，異類或時可得。若於過去，即可分別。如此如是，曾有相貌可分別故。非唯曾更而可分別。未曾更者，雖不分明取其相貌，然隨種類亦可分別。此則顯示，依現在行分別為因，生諸雜染。行雖無始然始可得者，顯示雜染時分差別。無始時來常隨逐故，剎那剎那新所起故。自此已後，顯清淨品。如實觀時得清淨故。或由自相故。謂觀色等如聚沫等。或由共相故。謂觀有為同生住滅所有共相。或由世俗及勝義諦故。謂雖無癡者，非無愚癡。眾緣所生世俗諦故，說癡能癡。又復顯示非不愚者不正思惟，是故彼為愚癡所癡。又由世俗，宣說諸識隨福等行。若就勝義，無所隨逐。又三應知者，謂去來今。三種業者，謂身等業。一切不和合者，更互相望不和合故。所以者何？現在速滅壞，過去住無方未生依眾緣，而復心隨轉。若彼與此更互相應、如福等行無有和合，彼心相應道理亦爾，云何當有實隨轉性？何以故？若心與彼諸行相應，或不相應；非此與彼或時不相應，或時非不相應。又非一切心或相應，或不相應。如是由勝義故，心隨轉性不得成就。今當顯示由世俗故，說心隨轉所有因緣。「於此流無斷」者，今此頌中，顯世俗諦非無作用及與隨轉。又由勝義，無有作者及與受者；由世俗故，而得宣說自作自受。又作者、受者若一若異皆不可說。為顯此義，故次說言前後差別等頌。

blocks.text: The prose commentary continues. Again, **almost all of today's Chinese is untranslated** (from 0364c15). The commentary below summarises it. It explains verses 10–26, which you read on Day 128.

(Partly translated.) Verses 10–11 show that ignorance and craving are "dharmas with causes": the defilement of householders and renunciants alike has causes. The next five verses show defilement's distinctions, supports, causes, and timing. "Dharmas with causes" are ignorance through feeling; "sufferings with causes" are craving through old age and death. These three groups correspond to the three defilements of affliction, karma, and birth (Day 53).

items: **"Because of two root afflictions"** points to afflictive defilement, taking only its strongest forms.

**Karmic defilement.** "It has no power of its own": a deed depends on good or bad friends who lead one. "Nor is it made by another": it depends on one's own effort. "No other can make it": it depends on the distinctions of prior causes. Karma is neither purely self-caused nor imposed.

**Where defilement arises.** "Not within, not without": defilement does not arise from future formations, which have no marks to discriminate; it arises from present and past formations. The past can be discriminated because its marks were experienced; even what was not personally experienced can be discriminated by its kind. So defilement arises from discriminating present formations.
**When.** "Though formations are beginningless, a beginning can be found": defilement has followed us since beginningless time, yet it is also newly arising moment by moment.

**Purification begins.** "From here on, the purified side is shown": one is purified by seeing as it truly is: by own marks (contemplating form and the rest as like foam), by shared marks (seeing all conditioned things arise, abide, and cease together), and by the two truths. Conventionally, delusion "deludes"; ultimately, there is no deluder. Conventionally, consciousness follows merit and demerit; ultimately, nothing follows. "The three" are past, future, and present; "three kinds of karma" are of body, speech, and mind; "nothing combines" because they never meet: the present ceases quickly, the past has no location, the future depends on conditions. If consciousness truly "followed" formations, it would be always associated with them, which it is not; so, ultimately, its "following" is not established.

blocks.text: This passage applies the two truths precisely. Conventionally, we may say karma is carried, consciousness follows merit, and the deluded are deluded. Ultimately, there is only the momentary arising of conditioned dharmas. Tomorrow's reading shows how, without a self, there can still be "doing and receiving".

quiz.q: "Nothing produces its own action, because it depends on being drawn out by good or bad companions." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: good friends lead to good karma, bad to bad — though one's own seed is the cause, other conditions must draw it out
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: guided by good friends one does good, by bad friends evil — though one's own seed is the cause, other conditions must draw it out. f16 omits the heading that this concerns karmic defilement.

quiz.q: "Nor is it produced by another, because it depends on one's own effort." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: a friend may guide you, but you must decide; if you don't act, the friend can do nothing
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Your friend leads you to do something, but you must decide before you can do it; if you won't, your friend can do nothing." Effort and conditions must combine.

quiz.q: The English renders 前生因 as "prior cause from an earlier life." How do the Pixunji and lectures read 前生?
options: once the prior link has arisen, it conditions the next — the preceding link in the sequence, not a past life
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "Apart from seed and conditions, nothing else can act — this is 'nor anything else.' Only once the prior link has arisen can it condition the next." Venerable Miào Jìng: this is "this being, that is."

quiz.q: The note frames §17 as the "fourfold refutation." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say the fourth line, "yet the function is not absent," means?
options: there are only three negations; "function not absent" corresponds to "the inconceivable ripening of results" — neither self nor other nor anything else acts, yet results arise
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Self doesn't act, other doesn't act, nothing else acts — then why are there results? There are results; this is inconceivable." The note's "fourfold refutation" misframes the passage.

quiz.q: What simile from the Saṃyukta, spoken by Mahākauṣṭhila, does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: three reeds leaning together — name-and-form and consciousness stand only by leaning on each other
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Name-and-form and consciousness are like reeds; they must lean on each other to stand." He reads the consciousness here as the store-consciousness.
